title: The Puddle on the Road
subtitle: The road ahead is long. Try not to let it soak your shoes.

trails.title: Chance Interview
trails.description: When an interview opportunity presents itself, a professional journalist always grabs it with both hands.

content.text:
Tuesday: An interview, huh? Well, I do declare, that is new ground for me, especially being interviewed by a child like you.
Tuesday: So, what do you want to know?
Barbara: You're no stranger to the realm of fear, and undoubtedly hold a unique perspective on the concept. That's why I want to hear what you have to say.
Tuesday: You're a curious little thing, aren't you? I wonder ... is the rest of your flock this nosy? Look, darling, for me, fear's just a little hobby. Like, some people enjoy fishing, some like brewing their own beer, and ... some even like combing the knots out of sheep fleece—no offense.
Barbara: None taken. Please, go on.
Tuesday: Appreciating fear takes finesse ... you have to ease into it gently, like nudging a glass along the edge of a table with just your fingertip.
Tuesday: Then, you hear that nice, crisp—clink.
Barbara: So, you see yourself as a fear facilitator, not a direct participant, correct?
Tuesday: You're a smart child.
Tuesday: How do I put this ... It's more like the scared are scaring themselves. Those poor lambs will do the hard work for you, you see. Their imagination is my greatest tool.
Tuesday: People start to make choices for themselves after experiencing true fear, based entirely on their imagination and of their own volition. And that's the most interesting part.

items.text: The sounds of the world fade into total silence, and when she opens her eyes again, there is nothing but darkness.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Where am I?
*plop*
A cool drop of water falls on her nose.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is that rain?

items.speaker: "The Ring"
items.text: I can catch anything with a toss.

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: Vertin, that's why you've gathered us here, right?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You shouldn't be here.

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: You understand what we desire most, right, Vertin?
The falling rain surrounds them. The children watch curiously.

items.speaker: "The Ring"
items.text: Vertin, we made it, right?

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: But why is it still raining?

items.speaker: "The Ring"
items.text: Don't be such a baby, Isabella. Haven't you seen rain before?
The children reach out as they try to catch the raindrops in their hands.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No!

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Are you afraid of children? Or rain?
A familiar voice echoes in the darkness.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, I'm not afraid of them.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Rain is common. It's always falling somewhere in the world.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's merely an ordinary weather phenomenon.
The maid snaps her fingers. The raindrops halt, then start to flow upward.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: This is the kind of rain you're afraid of, isn't it?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Hmm, I've never seen rain fall upwards. Is this some creation of your imagination? Still, I don't see why you'd be afraid of rain falling in reverse.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Would you care to enlighten me, dear child?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Tuesday, please. Stop trying to get in my head, and tell me where Argus is.
The maid ignores her and steps closer.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Before I met you, I never thought that a person without fear could exist in the world.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I've never once guessed someone's fear incorrectly, either. You really are something else.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You didn't guess incorrectly.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: These reversed raindrops have brought utter chaos to the world, pulverizing people under the crushing wheel of time.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You should be thankful you've never seen it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But it can't stop us anymore.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Because the umbrella's here.
She opens the umbrella.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: At least now, when the "Storm" comes, I can hold up the umbrella and protect my companions.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And although this ability has come too late for some, we still have a future to protect.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Why are you so obsessed with people's fears? Your hands have been trembling with excitement this whole time.
The maid clasps her hands under her chin, her face flushed like a blooming flower.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Haha. So I wasn't wrong at all.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Why waste your time with that mercenary? She may look tough, but she's hollow inside. Have you ever eaten a macadamia nut? Crack the hard shell, and you'll find the delicious center.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Who could resist the soft texture and rich flavor of fear?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Tuesday, this has to end.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You're the one pulling the strings here, aren't you?
The maid blushes as she twirls her skirt with one hand.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, what an astounding accusation.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: But, oh, do I feel so, so gratified. I've never felt so satiated in my entire life!
Her very being seems to be caught in a strange tremor.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Oh, you! You're the only one who's ever seen through me! How exhilarating!

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: However, your accusation missed the mark.
She stretches out her hands. They look especially pure under the rain.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: You see my hands? They're immaculate—never once tainted by a single drop of blood.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I take great pride in it. You see, I barely do anything to make people's fears arise.
Her hands tremble with excitement.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Ha, I would never injure anyone. Fear created through physical harm is its crudest and most base form.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: What I crave is the fear that lingers in their hearts forever.
The maid's cheeks flush a faint pink.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: The kind of fear that, even years later, when they recount their experiences here to their friends and families, a seed of fear is planted in the listeners' hearts.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Ahh, haha.

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: I instill fear in my guests, and they become my beloved children.
In the rain, her fingers tremble uncontrollably, and a beautiful smile spreads across her wet face.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Where is she? Where's Argus?

items.speaker: Tuesday
items.text: Well, I suppose she's experiencing her own fears right now. Under that hard mercenary exterior, she's tormented by them. Can you imagine that?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sorry, Ms. Tuesday.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But I'm not interested in this vile obsession of yours.
The one with the umbrella walks deeper into the darkness.
The sound of birds chirping fills the air. Argus is back home—on those familiar plains.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: This is ...
She stands in the field, nothing but the wind and the rustling grass before her.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Howdy, Argus, long time no see. We thought you'd never come back.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Mr. Dennis? Why are you here?

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Oh boy, you listening to yourself? Why wouldn't I be here?

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: It's my daughter's wedding day!

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Huh? W-Well, congratulations.
She finally catches on.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: But, you really shouldn't be here.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Don't you remember? Three years ago, your daughter ran away from home.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: She left a letter and then went with Mr. Shaffer to a city in the northeast, Detroit, I think? I don't quite remember.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Oh, come on, quit fooling around.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: After three months of searching, I found her, but she refused to come back with me. So, you went to Detroit yourself.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: And then, you ...
Her words drift off.
Dennis died in Detroit while looking for his daughter. At least, that's what she remembers.
But, how can that be? He's right here, standing in front of her.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: In any case, I'm sorry I couldn't bring her back.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: What're you talking about, Argus?

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: You must be tired from working on all those requests that the townsfolk have pushed upon you. I've told them so many times to go easy on you!

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: That said, I have a request for you myself!

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: What is it? Did you lose some livestock or—
The townsman winks and hands her an invitation.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Come to Alice's wedding!

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: We've prepared plenty of food and beer. And we've got the chapel choir together. Don't miss out, missy!

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Sorry, I won't be there.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Why?
Why, Argus?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I-I need to deliver a letter to, to Mrs. Mary's husband. She can't go herself because of her bad legs, you see.

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: Hey, Argus. I didn't ask you to deliver any letters.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Mrs. Mary, didn't you ...?
Mary passed away in 1989. Argus saw her coffin being lowered into the ground.
Another person declared dead is now standing before her, smiling brightly.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: You're still alive?

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: What kind of nonsense are you spouting?! You really ought to take a proper rest.

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: Today's Alice's big day. We should all be at her wedding, don't you think?

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: Oh, my sweet child, why are your hands shaking?

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: Are you afraid? Why?

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: Are you afraid of their happiness?

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: Or are you afraid of your failure?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I'm not a failure!

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: Oh, my sweet child.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Argus! Argus! Got a message to send? Go get Argus, your trusted friend!

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: Argus! Argus! Got a cheating spouse to catch? Go get Argus; she's got your back!
Argus ... Argus ...
A foreign voice echoes through their mouths and surrounds her.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Who's there?!
Her surroundings recede like a tide, leaving only a girl in white standing before her.
Wrapped in a half-soiled birth cloth, a lamb lies at her feet. The girl's hands are covered in blood and amniotic fluid. Her smile is as pure as a dove.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: It's me, Kayla. You haven't forgotten me, have you?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Kayla ...

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: It's getting dark. We should take them back. Ain't no way they'll make it through the night out here with their mama hurt.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: And you can't see a thing at night.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Yeah, we need to go back now. Can't delay any longer.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Oh.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Hold on a moment.
The lamb bleats.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: What are you doing?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: There, there.
She kneels down and gently strokes the lamb's neck. The lamb bows its head and licks her fingertips. They're still wet with amniotic fluid.
Kayla smiles and tightens her grip around the lamb's neck. It lets out a piercing cry, sending a distant flock of birds into the air.
The cry becomes weaker, more strangled, and then silent as the life is squeezed out of its body.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Isn't it better to die a quick death than end up in the belly of a wolf?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: You've got no right to make that decision.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: No living thing is born to simply die. It could've stood up. It could've survived.
The girl gets to her feet.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: We can go now.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: No, don't go.
The girl smiles as the long grass rustles against her flowing skirt in the breeze.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Oh, you've reminded me.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: There are two problems left unsolved. Those two over there.
Argus looks into the distance. Dennis and Mary are standing and smiling at her.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Kill them. It would only take two bullets. Three seconds max.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: As long as they're alive, they'll come after you just as hard as you hunt the targets of your missions.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: I'm sure you know that better than I do.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Why should I kill them?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Do you need a reason?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Just do as we've always done. I say, and you do. No need to think about it. Isn't that what you pride yourself on?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: A mindless tool that blindly follows orders. That's all a mercenary needs to be.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Isn't that the so-called value of a mercenary that you always talk about?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: No, it ain't true.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: What's with the hesitation, anyway? It's not like you give a damn about other people's lives.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: The only reason you can't bring yourself to kill them is because you enjoy how they always praise you and depend on you.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: You ain't Kayla.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Seriously? Are you saying I'm a fraud just because I don't meet your expectations of what I'm supposed to be?
The girl gives an inexplicable smile.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Fine. If you think I'm not Kayla, then why don't you kill me now?

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Just shoot me in the chest, and these people will treat you like a hero. They'll gather in the fields, holding torches, and chant your name.
Argus abruptly raises her gun, but her hands are shaking—the barrel trembling.

items.speaker: Kayla
items.text: Argus! Argus! She's—
*bang*
Argus! Argus!
The bullet pierces the girl's soft chest. Her blood splatters on the field, dotting the grass like a smattering of poppies.
It clings to the grass, its weight causing the blades to bend.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Oh, Argus! Our great hero!

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: The tales of your heroic deeds will be passed down through generations!

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: She ain't Kayla.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Now, now, you're lying to yourself again. Of course she's Kayla!

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: It's not possible.

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: Do I need to show you the bullet through her heart for you to believe it, bonehead?!

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Damn it!
She loads a bullet into the chamber with a crisp click.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Don't pull the trigger!
An unexpected voice comes from beside her.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Vertin?
How did she get all the way out here? Where did she come from?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Calm down, Argus.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Remember, what you see isn't real. You're still inside the motel, at least for now.

items.speaker: Resident I
items.text: Oh, here comes another little lady.

items.speaker: Resident II
items.text: Excellent timing. Come join the party!

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Vertin?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm here to get you out.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: So, that wasn't Kayla.
She lets out a long sigh of relief.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Couldn't ask for better news than that, really.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No, it wasn't.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's get out of here.
She reaches out her hand in invitation.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Okay.
Argus reaches out. She feels like something abominable is chasing after her—that if she stops, the shadow of confusion will come and swallow her whole.
And this hand is her only salvation—her escape from this labyrinth—so she grasps it tightly.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: She ain't Kayla.
She declares this with absolute certainty.
